desc: Analyze the parity structure: a valid alternating permutation must alternate odds/evens, so determine feasible starting parity and available odds/evens.
Derive the completion-count formula: O!*E! when a valid alternation from the required parity is feasible, else 0.

Implement the iterative greedy selection loop over candidates in ascending order using the completion-count formula, handling the first position (both parities allowed) and subsequent positions (required parity only).
Handle the global feasibility/k-out-of-range check, returning [] when total valid permutations < k.
Verify solution against provided examples (n=4,k=6 -> [3,4,1,2]; n=3,k=2 -> [3,2,1]; n=2,k=3 -> []) and edge cases (n=1,k=1 -> [1]; n=1,k=2 -> []).
Fall back to mixed-radix/factorial-number-system approach if greedy fails (not needed: greedy verified correct).
